challenges.name: non-idempotent-consumer-quiz
challenges.title: Which points were added twice?
challenges.description: The wallet consumer an AI wrote, hit by a crash between commit and ack, and a proposed fix that deduplicates on offsets.

questions.question:
Handler (from the AI), on a queue that redelivers unacked messages:
await pg.query("UPDATE wallets SET balance = balance + $2 WHERE user_id = $1", [e.userId, e.amount]);
await msg.ack();

wallets before: u-44 balance = 120
11:30:02.101  wallet-1  handled p-7720 (u-44, +30), transaction committed
11:30:02.102  kubelet   wallet-1 OOMKilled
11:30:12.400  wallet-3  received p-7720 (redelivered)
11:30:12.415  wallet-3  handled p-7720 (u-44, +30), transaction committed, acked

Statement: "u-44 now has a balance of 180, although event p-7720 awarded 30 points once."
questions.explanation: True. wallet-1 committed the UPDATE (120 + 30 = 150) and died before the ack, so the queue still considered p-7720 unprocessed and delivered it again. wallet-3 ran the same UPDATE on the committed balance: 150 + 30 = 180. The transaction made each delivery atomic, but nothing recorded that p-7720 had already been applied, and balance = balance + amount adds again on every delivery. The misconception is that a committed transaction plus an ack after it is enough; the window between commit and ack is exactly where duplicates come from.

False. An offset identifies a position in the log, not an event. The relay's second publish wrote p-9001 at a new, higher offset, so 7710 > 7709 and the handler applies the 50 points again. Storing offsets transactionally protects against the broker replaying the same positions (as after a rebalance), but not against a producer that publishes the same event twice, nor against a queue that redelivers a message after newer ones. Deduplicate on the event id the producer assigned, recorded in the same transaction as the balance change. The misconception is that a duplicate always has the same offset.

challenges.name: spot-the-ai-mistake-points-twice
challenges.title: Spot the AI Mistake: a consumer that adds points twice
challenges.description:
An AI coding assistant was asked: "write a consumer that adds the points from `points.awarded` events to the wallet balance". It wrote `WalletConsumer`: it validates the payload, adds `amount` to the balance inside a transaction, and its tests, one delivery per event, pass. After a deploy restarted the consumers and the consumer group rebalanced, messages that had been processed but not acked were delivered again, and learners reported that their points had doubled; the leaderboard reads these balances.

Fix `WalletConsumer` so that every `points.awarded` event changes the balance exactly once, however many times and in whatever order it is delivered, across crashes and restarts:
- `handle(msg)` returns "applied" the first time an event id changes a balance, "duplicate" (no change) for an event id that already changed it, and "invalid" (no change) when `msg.id` or `payload.userId` is not a non-empty string or `payload.amount` is not a positive integer;
- two different events with the same user and amount are two awards: both are applied;
- the tests may crash the process just before or just after the commit of the transaction that changes `wallets`, and a rebalance or a crash hands the partition to a new `WalletConsumer` on the same database (anything kept in the consumer object is lost); a message that was not acked comes again, possibly after newer ones.

Accepted protocols: record the event id in `processed_events` (an inbox), or in `points_ledger` (a ledger keyed by event id from which the balance follows), in the same `db.tx` as the change to `wallets`. The runner prints only what `handle` returns and the final balances, so either protocol gives the same output. Never catch `Crash`.

Input (JSON): a list of steps: `{ "deliver": { "id", "userId", "amount" }, "crash"?: "beforeCommit" | "afterCommit" }` or `{ "rebalance": true }`. Output: one line per delivery (`<id> <user> +<amount>: applied, acked` / `duplicate, acked` / `invalid, acked` / `crashed before commit, not acked` / `crashed after commit, not acked`), a line per rebalance, then `wallets: <user>=<balance> ...`. The public tests pass on the AI's code; the hidden tests deliver duplicates, reorder them and crash before the ack.
hints: When the same event id arrives a second time, possibly at a new consumer after a rebalance, what in the database could tell the handler that its points are already in the balance?

Look at the transaction in handle: it changes wallets but writes nothing about msg.id. The schema already has processed_events and points_ledger. Which one would you write in that same transaction, what must happen when the id is already there, and what can you do with a message that has no id?

A similar consumer grants badges: badge.granted b-12 for u5. In one transaction it inserts b-12 into its processed table; if b-12 was already there it returns duplicate and changes nothing, otherwise it adds the badge. Deliveries b-12, b-13, a restart, then b-12 again give applied, applied, duplicate, and u5 has 2 badges. A crash before that transaction commits leaves no trace, so the next b-12 is applied.

tests.name: One delivery per event: the balances add up
tests.expected:
p1 u1 +50: applied, acked
p2 u2 +20: applied, acked
p3 u1 +30: applied, acked
wallets: u1=80 u2=20

tests.name: Two awards with the same user and amount are two awards
tests.expected:
p1 u1 +50: applied, acked
p2 u1 +50: applied, acked
p3 u2 +10: applied, acked
wallets: u1=100 u2=10

tests.name: Invalid payloads (zero, negative, fractional amount, no user) change nothing
tests.expected:
p1 u1 +0: invalid, acked
p2 u1 +-5: invalid, acked
p3 u1 +2.5: invalid, acked
p4 (no user) +10: invalid, acked
p5 u1 +10: applied, acked
wallets: u1=10

tests.name: Rebalance: processed but unacked events come again and change nothing
tests.expected:
p1 u1 +50: applied, acked
p2 u2 +20: applied, acked
p3 u1 +30: applied, acked
p4 u3 +100: applied, acked
rebalance: partition assigned to a new consumer
p3 u1 +30: duplicate, acked
p4 u3 +100: duplicate, acked
p5 u2 +10: applied, acked
wallets: u1=80 u2=30 u3=100

tests.name: Crash after commit, before ack: the redelivery is a duplicate
tests.expected:
p1 u1 +50: crashed after commit, not acked
p1 u1 +50: duplicate, acked
p2 u1 +20: applied, acked
p2 u1 +20: duplicate, acked
wallets: u1=70

tests.name: Out of order: an event that crashed before commit returns after newer events
tests.expected:
p1 u1 +50: crashed before commit, not acked
p2 u1 +20: applied, acked
p3 u2 +10: applied, acked
p1 u1 +50: applied, acked
p2 u1 +20: duplicate, acked
wallets: u1=70 u2=10

tests.name: A message without an event id cannot be deduplicated and is rejected
tests.expected:
(no id) u1 +50: invalid, acked
(no id) u1 +50: invalid, acked
p1 u1 +50: applied, acked
wallets: u1=50
